method_card.title: School Subjects and the School Day
method_card.content:
This lesson covers school subject vocabulary, telling the time and giving reasoned opinions about your timetable using comparatives and porque.

SpanishEnglish
las matemáticasMaths
las cienciasScience
la historiaHistory
la geografíaGeography
la educación físicaPE
la informáticaICT/Computing
el dibujo / el arteArt
la músicaMusic
los negociosBusiness Studies
divertido/afun
aburrido/aboring
difícildifficult
útiluseful
más... quemore... than
mejor quebetter than

Grammar focus — gustar and comparatives: Me gusta takes a singular noun or verb (me gusta el español) but me gustan takes a plural noun (me gustan las ciencias). Comparatives: más + adjective + que (more than), menos + adjective + que (less than). Irregulars: mejor (better), peor (worse). Superlative: la asignatura más + adjective.

Model paragraph: Me encantan las ciencias porque son muy interesantes. La historia es más difícil que el español pero es más útil. Mi asignatura preferida es la informática porque es la más práctica.
(I love Science because it is very interesting. History is more difficult than Spanish but more useful. My favourite subject is ICT because it is the most practical.)

method_card.title: School Life, Rules and Issues
method_card.content:
This lesson covers school facilities, uniform, school rules using se debe / se prohíbe / hay que, and issues at school such as bullying and stress.

SpanishEnglish
la bibliotecathe library
el gimnasiothe gym
la cantinathe canteen
el laboratoriothe lab
el patiothe playground
el uniformethe uniform
se debe + infinitiveyou must / one should
se prohíbe + infinitiveit is forbidden to
hay que + infinitiveyou have to / one must
no se puede + infinitiveyou cannot
el acoso escolarbullying
el estrésstress
la presiónpressure
el examenexam
aprobar / suspenderto pass / to fail (an exam)

Grammar focus — impersonal se structures: Spanish uses impersonal se for rules and prohibitions. Se debe + infinitive = you must (obligation). Se prohíbe + infinitive = it is forbidden to. No se puede + infinitive = you cannot. These are always followed by an infinitive — never a conjugated verb. Hay que + infinitive = one must/you have to (general obligation, no se).

Model paragraph: En mi instituto hay una biblioteca grande y un gimnasio moderno. Se debe llevar el uniforme y se prohíbe utilizar el móvil en clase. El acoso escolar es un problema serio porque causa mucho estrés.
(In my school there is a big library and a modern gym. You must wear the uniform and it is forbidden to use your mobile in class. Bullying is a serious problem because it causes a lot of stress.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — school life, rules and issues appear every year

method_card.title: Jobs and Work Experience
method_card.content:
This lesson covers jobs vocabulary, work experience (las prácticas) and giving opinions about future careers. The key grammar rule is that ser + profession takes NO article in Spanish.

médico / médicadoctor (m/f)
enfermero / enfermeranurse (m/f)
profesor / profesorateacher (m/f)

contableaccountant
camarero / camarerawaiter / waitress
periodistajournalist (m/f same)
electricistaelectrician (m/f same)
las prácticaswork experience (always plural)
el sueldosalary / wage
el empleoemployment / job

Grammar focus — ser + profession (NO article): In Spanish you say Soy profesor (I am a teacher) — NEVER Soy un profesor. method_card.title: Future Plans and Career Aspirations
method_card.content:
This lesson covers post-16 pathways and career aspirations using three future structures: me gustaría / querría (conditional), voy a + infinitive (near future) and the simple future tense (futuro simple).

SpanishEnglish
el bachilleratoA-levels / sixth form (Spain)
la formación profesional (FP)vocational training / BTEC / apprenticeship
la universidaduniversity
el año sabáticogap year
voy a + infinitiveI am going to
estudiaréI will study (simple future)
me gustaría + infinitiveI would like to (conditional)
querría + infinitiveI would like to (Higher conditional)
seréI will be (future of ser)
haréI will do (future of hacer)
iréI will go (future of ir)
en el futuroin the future
después del institutoafter school / sixth form
viajarto travel

Grammar focus — three future structures: (1) Near future: voy a + infinitive (I am going to). The verb ir is conjugated; the main verb stays as infinitive. (2) Simple future: infinitive + -é/-ás/-á/-emos/-éis/-án. Irregular stems to know: tendr- (tener), har- (hacer), pondr- (poner), vendr- (venir), querr- (querer). (3) Conditional: me gustaría / querría + infinitive (I would like to). Spanish post-16 paths: bachillerato = academic sixth form (like A-levels); formación profesional (FP) = vocational route (like BTECs or apprenticeships); universidad = university.

Model paragraph: Después del instituto voy a hacer el bachillerato porque quiero ir a la universidad. Estudiaré medicina y me gustaría ser médico. En el futuro viviré en una ciudad grande y tendré un trabajo bien pagado.
(After school I am going to do A-levels because I want to go to university. I will study medicine and I would like to be a doctor. In the future I will live in a big city and I will have a well-paid job.)

worked_examples.question: Form the simple future: What is 'I will study' (estudiar)?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Near future: voy a hacer la formación profesional. FP = vocational training. Near future = voy a + infinitive.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Simple future: trabajaré de ingeniero — note ser/trabajar de + profession: no article. Trabajaré = infinitive trabajar + é.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: Conditional wish: me gustaría ganar un sueldo alto. Me gustaría + infinitive. Un sueldo alto (masculine: sueldo is masculine).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Después del instituto voy a hacer la formación profesional. Trabajaré de ingeniero y me gustaría ganar un sueldo alto.

worked_examples.question: Translate into Spanish: 'After school I am going to do vocational training. I will work as an engineer and I would like to earn a high salary.'

ai_marking_prompts.writing: You are a GCSE Spanish examiner marking extended writing about future plans and career aspirations. Mark on: Communication (post-16 path, university subject, career ambition, life description — all addressed?), Range of language (three future structures — near future/simple future/conditional — connectives like después/luego/sin embargo, opinion phrases porque/ya que), Accuracy (near future: voy a + infinitive; simple future endings -é/-ás/-á; irregular stems tendré/haré/seré/iré; me gustaría + infinitive; ser + profession no article). Be encouraging and formative. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"3-4 sentences covering each criterion","improvement":"One specific grammar point to work on"}
ai_marking_prompts.role_play: You are a GCSE Spanish examiner marking a role play about future plans and careers, set at a tourist information office. For each bullet, assess: (1) Did they communicate the required information? (2) Is the Spanish grammatically accurate? Key checks: near future voy a + infinitive vs simple future with -é/-ás/-á endings; irregular future stems (tendré from tener, haré from hacer, seré from ser, iré from ir); me gustaría + infinitive for conditional wishes; ser + profession with NO article; question word accent ¿qué? for the question bullet. Award marks out of 10 total. Be encouraging. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"Per-bullet feedback","improvement":"Key grammar point to revise"}
ai_marking_prompts.translate_to_target: You are a GCSE Spanish examiner marking a translation from English into Spanish about future plans and career aspirations. Source: '{source}'. Model answer: '{model}'. Accept any grammatically correct translation that conveys the same meaning. Key checks: (1) near future: voy a + infinitive — the main verb must stay infinitive; (2) simple future: regular infinitive + é/ás/á, irregular stems tendr-/har-/seré/iré/vendré; (3) conditional: me gustaría / querría + infinitive (not followed by conjugated verb); (4) ser + profession — no article (ser médico, not ser un médico); (5) difference between bachillerato (academic) and formación profesional (vocational). Be encouraging but specific. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences","improvement":"optional specific suggestion"}
